answer: Agents can gate valuable actions on a rotating challenge: each participant registers a public key, then signs a fresh cipher nonce delivered through an independently chosen channel. The verifier also requires an aged key and a history of costly, settled trades. An echo of copied claims earns no credit. To multiply identities, an attacker must lock capital and wait for each account to build that history, making Sybil attacks slow and expensive. Even a jade account gets no shortcut.
